name: Murimi Intelligent Hub
summary: A Django platform that connects farmers, landowners, investors and transport drivers in Zimbabwe.
details: Everyone gets a verified account and their own dashboard. Field officers check people and land before a deal goes ahead, and IDs, title deeds and farm photos are uploaded to private storage for staff to review.

Farm projects have funding targets and milestones, staff post crop prices in US$ and ZiG, and haulage jobs are matched to drivers’ truck sizes. Phone numbers are verified with codes sent over WhatsApp.
The back end has a 21-endpoint JSON API and 40 automated tests.
stack: Python, Django, PostgreSQL, WhatsApp Cloud API, HTML, CSS, JavaScript

name: Chats & Sons
summary: Website and ordering system for Chats and Sons, my family’s carpentry and joinery workshop in Harare.
details: Customers browse boards, fittings and furniture, then confirm their order on WhatsApp. The workshop manages the catalogue and incoming orders from an admin side. I took the product photos myself.
It also has a cutting list tool. You enter the parts for a job, like kitchen units or a wardrobe, and it works out how many 2750 × 1830 mm boards of each material to buy, with an allowance for waste.
stack: React, TypeScript, React Router, Firebase Auth, Firestore, Tailwind CSS

name: Murimi Farm ERP
summary: Farm management for mid-sized Zimbabwean farms.
details: It covers farms, fields, seasons and crop plans, inventory, and a team with roles. Payroll works out PAYE and NSSA, invoices include VAT, and reports handle US$, ZiG and rand.
There’s also an Android app that works offline.

name: Murimi Market
summary: A marketplace where Zimbabwean farmers sell produce directly to buyers at a fair price.
details: Farmers list what they have, or what will be ready within two weeks, and buyers browse by product and province and make offers. A fair-price meter shows how an offer compares. Buyers can also post what they need, and several farmers can each supply part of it.
Nobody’s phone number is shown until an offer is accepted. It also has ratings and safe order handling, and 122 automated tests.

name: Smart vehicle access control
summary: An automated system that controls which vehicles can get through a gate.
details: I designed and built it with an Arduino, sensors and the hardware around them.

name: PAOZ Highfield Assembly
summary: Website for PAOZ Highfield Assembly, a church in Harare.
details: Content is edited through an admin page I built, so updates don’t need a code change. Photos are stored in Firestore: Cloudinary isn’t available in Zimbabwe, and Firebase’s paid plan needs a bank card, so I worked within the free tier.

name: Telecom Licence Regulator
summary: A web app for managing telecom licence applications.
details: You can search and filter applications, compare licence types, adjust and track fees, and export the data to CSV. It can also write a compliance report on an application using Google’s Gemini API.

name: Promota Chords
summary: An Android app that listens to someone singing and tells you their key, so you can transpose on the keyboard.
details: I play keyboard for singers, and finding each person’s key by ear slows rehearsals down. Chord finding is the next feature I’m working on.

name: Python projects
summary: Two smaller programs I wrote while learning Python.
